approach: Add one prose section to the producer brief, built by a new helper `source_check_section()` in `crates/athena-context/src/briefs/boundary.rs`. The helper sits beside `mirror_check_section()` and uses the same constant-plus-helper pattern. `producer_brief_with_evidence` in `briefs.rs` writes it right after `mirror_check_section()` and before "## Checks Athena will run". That function builds every producer brief (fresh, seeded retry, resume, stale-conflict, unseeded retry, with or without evidence), so retries get the section too. The text tells the producer, for every term, claim, count or list its change writes about named sources, to do four things. First, search every governing source with Grep, not the first hit. Second, list every sense of the term found and say which sense it used. Third, compare any hand-kept list with the file that defines it, entry by entry. Fourth, state in its `criteria_check` evidence what it did not check. A new unit test asserts the section is in the fresh brief, in each retry shape and in the with-evidence brief, in the right place and with its key phrases. Removing the call makes the test panic. A decision entry D190 is appended to docs/decisions.md and a bullet is added to CHANGELOG.md. No check, gate, admission, landing, config, workflow or prompt-file change, so no refusal rule is added.

decisions.choice: Put the text in the producer brief as a section built by a helper, with a unit test on the rendered brief. Do not add a refusal rule.
decisions.reason: The root cause is that the brief never says it. The brief is the place a producer reads before writing. The user's default 'mechanism' is met because the section is produced by code and a test pins that it reaches every brief shape. The request and the out-of-scope list rule out a gate on contradicted terms.

rejected.option: A refusal or gate rule that rejects work containing a contradicted term
rejected.why: Out of scope. It would be a matching rule needing a refusal corpus and a replay. The reading says to add none.
The producer prompt set is at 1043 of 1200 (docs/system-facts.md). The criteria also forbid any prompt .md under crates/*/prompts/. A brief section has no token budget.

decisions.choice: Place the section after `mirror_check_section()` and before '## Checks Athena will run'.
decisions.reason: The producer reads rules for what it writes (banned words, hand-kept files) in that block, before the checks (briefs.rs:695-697). The new section is the same kind of rule. Tests such as `producer_briefs_tell_the_producer_to_run_the_mirror_check` (briefs.rs:2679) already pin that block before the checks, so it is the established place.

rejected.why: Later sections concern checks and reporting. Advice about what to write is better read before the work, and the tail of the brief is already long.

decisions.choice: The section text avoids the phrases that existing brief tests ban: 'must address', 'rejected candidate', 'starts from the base', 'cost', '0.8', '0.97', 'p10', the Time-budget heading, and every boundary word.
decisions.reason: Negative assertions exist at briefs.rs:1631 (forecasts, including the substring 'cost'), 2253 ('must address' absent from a fresh brief), 2221 and 2309 (retry wording) and 2184-2190 (pacing text). The boundary scan also rejects banned words in any tracked file, so the wording must be checked against `boundary_words()`.

decisions.choice: Do not change docs/decision-links.toml. D190 is written without any 'Amends' or 'Supersedes' phrase.
decisions.reason: The new brief text does not revise a decision. [[governs]] lists only D08's two files (decision-links.toml:196-201), and neither is touched. An 'Amends ... in prose only' phrase with an `amended` link would be a claim the change does not make. The file is a listed deliverable only as a low-probability one.

rejected.option: Add an `amended` link to D73 or D184 so the deliverable list is met
rejected.why: It would assert an amendment that is not made, and the decision gate (D187) would then require the phrase and the link to agree.

files.purpose: Add `SOURCE_CHECK_INSTRUCTION` (a `pub(super)` const) and `pub(super) fn source_check_section() -> String`, placed after `mirror_check_section` (line 87-89). The heading is '## Check what you write against its sources'. The text tells the producer: when a file it writes summarizes, lists or defines something a named source governs, search every governing source with Grep (not only the first hit) for each term, claim, count or list it writes. List every sense of the term found and say which it used. Compare any hand-kept list with the file that defines it, entry by entry. State in `criteria_check` evidence what it did not check: a source not searched, a sense not read, a list not compared. It must avoid the banned words and the phrases listed under decisions.

Import `source_check_section` in the `use boundary::{...}` line (line 37). Add `let _ = writeln!(out, "{}", source_check_section());` after `mirror_check_section()` in `producer_brief_with_evidence` (line 696). Add the unit test `producer_brief_tells_the_producer_to_check_what_it_writes_against_every_source` to the `tests` module beside the existing-tests test (after line 4187).

Append (after the last line, no existing text edited) a blank line and the entry '## D190 · The producer brief tells the producer to check content that summarizes named sources against every source and every sense of a term'. It has the Case, Decision, Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal cost and Provenance bullets in the form of D189. The Case names the root cause for the class of job 20261114-045722-vbq4 (which recorded no candidate and no findings): the producer stage lacked an instruction to check such content against its sources for every sense of a term. The Provenance bullet lists what was read (`producer_brief_with_evidence`, `boundary.rs`) and what ran, and says not measured whether producers follow it. It has no 'Amends' or 'Supersedes' phrase.

Add one bullet at the top of '### Added' under '## [Unreleased]' (before line 37). It names job 20261116-034346-q8am (retry of 20261114-045722-vbq4), the root cause, the fix (`source_check_section` and its call, test name), limits (prose only, not measured whether producers follow it, no refusal rule), and D190.

steps: In crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs line 37 change the import to `use boundary::{banned_words_section, mirror_check_section, source_check_section};`.
In `producer_brief_with_evidence`, directly after `let _ = writeln!(out, "{}", mirror_check_section());` (line 696), add `let _ = writeln!(out, "{}", source_check_section());`.

In the `tests` module of briefs.rs, after `producer_brief_tells_the_producer_to_run_existing_tests_that_read_its_output` (ends line 4187), add `producer_brief_tells_the_producer_to_check_what_it_writes_against_every_source`. It builds the fresh, seeded-retry, stale-conflict, unseeded-retry and with-evidence briefs from `producer_inputs(None)`, `seed()` and `RetryFindings`. For each it cuts the section out with the same slice idiom as the existing-tests test, asserts the key phrases, asserts the section is after '## Files kept by hand' and before '## Checks Athena will run', asserts the heading appears once, and asserts no boundary word or fragment is in the section.

Run `cargo test -p athena-context`, then `cargo test -p athena-cli`, then `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test mirrors`. Fix any wording that a negative assertion or the scan rejects.

Append the D190 entry to docs/decisions.md after its last line (the end of D189's Provenance bullet), with a leading blank line, the heading `## D190 · ...`, and the Case/Decision/Alternatives/Tradeoff/Reversal cost/Provenance bullets. No existing line is edited. Do not write 'Amends', 'Supersedes' or 'Superseded by'.
Add the CHANGELOG.md bullet at the top of '### Added' under '## [Unreleased]'. Leave docs/decision-links.toml, athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows and prompts unchanged.

Run `cargo fmt --check`, then `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, then `cargo test`, each as its own command. Then run `git diff --stat` to confirm that only the four paths changed. Record each command in `criteria_check` evidence.

risks.risk: An existing brief test or the boundary scan rejects a word in the new text (for example the substring 'cost' at briefs.rs:1631).
risks.mitigation: The section is worded to avoid every phrase those tests ban, and the new test scans the section for boundary words. The producer runs `cargo test -p athena-context` and `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` before finishing. Do not use the words 'cost', 'lease', 'handoff', 'sandbox' or 'operator', or 'must address'.

risks.risk: The append breaks the decision-log rule (id, heading form, Provenance, append-only).
risks.mitigation: The entry is written to the end of the file with a leading blank line, and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test mirrors` is run to see the append-only and next-id rules pass. It must be D190, as D189 is the last id (decisions.md:5580).

risks.risk: A prose section may not change producer behavior.
risks.mitigation: State plainly in D190 and CHANGELOG that the section is prose only and that compliance is not measured. The test pins only that the text reaches every brief shape. A refusal rule is out of scope by the request.

risks.risk: docs/decision-links.toml is listed as an expected deliverable but the plan does not modify it.
risks.mitigation: The deliverable list marks decision-links.toml as low probability. The plan leaves it unchanged because no [[governs]] path is touched and D190 amends nothing. If the verifier requires it, the diff shows no change to a governed path or phrase, so no link is owed (decision-links.toml:24-32).

demonstrations.method: Content check by diff and by the existing decision-log rule. (a) git diff of docs/decisions.md shows only added lines, all after the old last line (the end of D189's Provenance bullet, decisions.md:5633). It adds a '## D190 · ...' entry with a Provenance bullet. The entry names the root cause (the producer brief had no instruction to check content summarizing named sources against every source and every sense of a term) and cites job 20261114-045722-vbq4 as recording no candidate and no findings. (b) git diff of CHANGELOG.md shows one added bullet under '## [Unreleased]' naming job 20261116-034346-q8am and its retry source. (c) `cargo test -p athena-cli --test mirrors` runs the registry's decision-log rule (`Rule::DecisionEntries`, mirrors.rs:23 and 346-396: next id, well-formed heading, Provenance bullet, append-only).
demonstrations.observes: A diff of decisions.md with no '-' lines other than the file header. D190 follows D189 with a Provenance bullet. The CHANGELOG bullet names the job. The mirrors test passes.

demonstrations.method: Content check by diff. boundary.rs gains `SOURCE_CHECK_INSTRUCTION` and `pub(super) fn source_check_section() -> String`, which returns the '## Check what you write against its sources' section. briefs.rs line 37 imports it next to `banned_words_section` and `mirror_check_section`. `producer_brief_with_evidence` gains `let _ = writeln!(out, "{}", source_check_section());` after the `mirror_check_section()` line (briefs.rs:696). The text, read in the diff, tells the producer to search each governing source for every term, claim or list it writes, list every sense found, compare any hand-kept list with the file that defines it, and state what it did not check.
demonstrations.observes: The added helper and its call in the diff, and the four instructions in the constant's text.

demonstrations.method: A new unit test in the `tests` module of briefs.rs, in the style of `producer_brief_tells_the_producer_to_run_existing_tests_that_read_its_output` (briefs.rs:4159). It builds briefs with the real production entry points: a fresh `producer_brief(&producer_inputs(None))`; a seeded retry (`retry_from = Some(seed())`); a stale-conflict retry (`seed()` with `conflicts` set); an unseeded retry (`retry_findings = Some(RetryFindings{..})`); and `producer_brief_with_evidence(&producer_inputs(None), Some("/tmp/ev"))`. For each it cuts the section out (heading to the next '\n## ') and asserts it contains the phrases 'every governing source', 'every sense', 'hand-kept list', 'did not check'. It asserts the section starts after '## Files kept by hand' and before '## Checks Athena will run'. It asserts the section holds none of the banned words or fragments (`boundary_words()`, `boundary_fragments()`) and that no retry brief has a second copy of the heading. The second command, `cargo test -p athena-context`, runs the whole crate, so the existing brief tests with negative assertions (briefs.rs:1631, 2184, 2221, 2253, 2309) are shown to still pass.
demonstrations.observes: The new test passes, and the whole athena-context crate passes. A copy with the call removed fails the new test with a panic at `.expect`.
demonstrations.fails_without: Delete the `writeln!(out, "{}", source_check_section())` line from `producer_brief_with_evidence`. `brief.find("## Check what you write against its sources")` then returns None and the test's `.expect(...)` panics for every brief shape. The only difference between the passing and failing runs is that call.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points `producer_brief` and `producer_brief_with_evidence` (briefs.rs:676, 682). Inputs come from the test helpers `producer_inputs(None)` (briefs.rs:2123), `seed()` (briefs.rs:2137) and `RetryFindings`, all of which exist today. No fake or double is used. The brief text is the real output and the assertions read it. The new test is added by step 4. `source_check_section` is added by step 1.

demonstrations.method: Run the whole athena-cli test suite. Of the crate's tests, only `job_plan.rs` (:259-275) and `lifecycle.rs` (:292) read a producer brief, and both read the brief the run itself wrote. job_plan.rs:270-275 builds the expected prompt from the stored brief and the plan section, so the new section appears on both sides. The `mirrors` test target (`cargo test -p athena-cli --test mirrors`) is part of the run.
demonstrations.observes: All athena-cli tests pass with the section in the brief.
demonstrations.fails_without: A test that compared a whole producer brief against fixed text would fail here. None was found: the crate's producer-brief readers (`job_plan.rs:259-275`, `lifecycle.rs:292`) take the stored brief from the run just made and compare it with the prompt the producer received.
demonstrations.seam: Existing tests drive `athena_core` dispatch with the fixture in crates/athena-cli/tests (exists today). They call the changed production function `producer_brief_with_evidence` at run/mod.rs:1198. No new seam.

demonstrations.method: Run, each as its own command, in this order: `cargo fmt --check`, then `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, then `cargo test`. Checks Athena runs on the result are `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`. A passing Athena-recorded run of these on the final tree counts. Reasons to expect clean runs: the new constant and function use only `format!`/string literals as `mirror_check_section` does, the helper is used (no dead-code lint), and the new constant is `pub(super)`, so no public API changes. Fixed text has no unusual escapes.
demonstrations.fails_without: A formatting slip or a clippy lint in the new function or test fails the matching command. A test broken in another crate by the extra section fails `cargo test`.
demonstrations.seam: Existing: the checks configured in athena.toml. No new seam.
